erd: After a shared early positive transient, mu power falls below baseline more strongly for fists at C3 (0–4 s mean -9.8%) and C4 (-4.7%) than for feet (+1.3% and -1.2%). At Cz, feet show only slightly more mean desynchronization (-2.2%) than fists (-0.6%), with substantial fluctuations. The stronger lateral fist response and weak medial foot contrast are broadly compatible with hand/foot somatotopy but do not provide a clean spatial dissociation. Weak Cz could reflect source mixing, reference choice, intersubject variation, noise or cue-related activity; this plot alone cannot identify the cause.
embedding: The figure uses the validation-selected original YourModel seed 0, preselected independently of test accuracy. Fixed-random-seed (0) t-SNE projects its 64-dimensional CLS embeddings from all 90 test trials; colors identify fists/feet and markers identify subjects 9/10. Axes are arbitrary t-SNE coordinates. It is a descriptive visualization of an already evaluated cohort, not a model-selection instrument: local neighborhoods and global distances can be distorted, and visible separation would not establish accuracy, statistical significance or physiological specificity. Visual inspection shows substantial overlap of the two class colors and both subject markers, without a clean class-separated cluster structure.
